end.summary:
Practised reading and plotting ordered pairs (x, y) on the Cartesian plane.
Harsh identified the origin and explained that it belongs to no quadrant.
They correctly identified (4, 3), (-4, -2), and Quadrant III from coordinate directions.
Harsh continued to treat (3, 2) and (2, 3) as the same point; this was not corrected after the last occurrence.
Teach-back on representing points in the Cartesian plane was not passed.
end.parentNote: Harsh practised plotting points by moving horizontally for x and vertically for y, including negative directions and quadrants. They used the origin and coordinate signs correctly in several examples, including identifying Quadrant III. The mix-up that (3, 2) and (2, 3) are the same point remained at the end of the lesson (correctAfterLastSeen: false). At home, draw a small grid and plot both points separately, checking that the first number always gives the horizontal move and the second gives the vertical move.
